'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
***[[Hamas]] hands the remains of three more dead hostages over to the [[Red Cross]] following the release of four bodies on Monday. Twenty-one bodies of hostages remain in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. A fourth body was found not to be a hostage.  [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cx2r2z0gyp7t (BBC News)] [https://www.thetimes.com/world/middle-east/article/gaza-ceasefire-live-hamas-hostages-israel-latest-news-9drvr9pcm (''The Times'')]
***[[Israel]]i forensic teams identify the four dead hostages returned on Monday as three [[Israelis]] and a [[Nepal]]ese citizen, all of whom were kidnapped during the [[October 7 attacks]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/14/world/middleeast/israeli-hostages-bodies-hamas.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx27ye11ey2o (BBC News)]
***In response to the limited release of bodies on Monday, Israel notifies the [[United Nations]] it will not open the [[Rafah Border Crossing|Rafah crossing]] and only allow 300 [[Gaza Strip famine|aid trucks]] to enter the Gaza Strip daily, instead of the 600 agreed to in the ceasefire agreement. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/hamas-fighters-tighten-grip-gaza-clouding-future-ceasefire-2025-10-14/ (Reuters)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israel-tells-un-it-will-only-allow-half-of-agreed-number-of-aid-trucks-into-gaza-after-hamas-ceasefire-violation/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli troops]] kill nine [[Palestinians]] in Gaza, saying those killed violated the IDF's withdrawal line as established by the peace agreement. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2025/10/14/live-trump-signs-gaza-ceasefire-deal-with-leaders-of-qatar-egypt-turkiye (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.thetimes.com/world/middle-east/article/gaza-latest-news-hostages-peace-trump-ceasefire-netanyahu-h2cds53gv (''The Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/hamas-fighters-tighten-grip-gaza-clouding-future-ceasefire-2025-10-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[War on drugs]], [[2025 US Caribbean naval deployment]]
**[[2025 United States strikes on Venezuelan boats]]
***The [[United States Navy]] carries out an airstrike on an alleged drug boat near the coast of [[Venezuela]]. [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that at least six people were killed by the attack. [https://apnews.com/article/trump-cartels-drugs-venezuela-boat-strike-af1a784864268707a76755a98615563e (AP)]
*[[Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria]]
**At least 13 people are killed and others are injured in attacks by suspected herders on two villages in [[Plateau State]], Nigeria. [https://english.news.cn/africa/20251016/95bf7ea056454215bd65f0b7c0b59f0e/c.html (Xinhua News Agency)]
*[[Ecuadorian conflict (2024–present)|Ecuadorian conflict]]
**At least one person is killed and several others are injured in a [[car bomb]] explosion near a shopping mall in [[Guayaquil]], [[Ecuador]]. [https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/10/car-bomb-explodes-near-shopping-mall-in-ecuadors-largest-city/ (BNO News)]
*[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] [[Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|government]] and the [[Rwanda]]-backed [[March 23 Movement|M23 rebels]] sign an agreement in [[Doha]], [[Qatar]], to formally establish an oversight body to work towards a permanent ceasefire, which will include representatives from the two groups and the other members of the [[International Conference on the Great Lakes Region]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-m23-sign-deal-doha-ceasefire-monitoring-sources-say-2025-10-14/ (Reuters)] [https://apnews.com/article/congo-m23-rwanda-ceasefire-fighting-6e31fee274c3ca2c3a79fdd76078d3e9 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[China–United States trade war]], [[China–South Korea relations]]
**The [[China|Chinese]] [[Ministry of Commerce (China)|commerce ministry]] issues sanctions on and bans Chinese companies from dealing with five subsidiaries of [[South Korea]]n shipbuilding company [[Hanwha Ocean]], which has [[shipyard]]s and investments in the United States and maintains contracts with the [[U.S. Navy]]. [https://apnews.com/article/china-us-hanwha-shipbuilding-korea-trade-cb72348bb00cb95801c2d6b5a47702fa (AP)] [https://www.wsj.com/business/china-adds-hanwha-oceans-units-to-sanctions-list-d99b1757?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=ASWzDAhLAanPSuBDcOGNf5PG3T7KG0E8XPs0slqdGShQKDZzGPE5Tx1oLflY&gaa_ts=68eeb80c&gaa_sig=R0EUpfrgbh-lfvfsAjxIn_VxSn3hjfdvxcnrc5e2Kg526u_9CKqkW_5xBIhLSj7-Z4vrjQ_zWgeY4q7JkGxtqA%3D%3D (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*The [[European Union]] fines [[luxury goods|luxury]] brands [[Gucci]], [[Chloé]], and [[Loewe (fashion brand)|Loewe]] over {{Euro}}157 million (US$182.5 million) for violating EU [[European Union competition law|competition law]]s through [[price fixing]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/eu-fines-gucci-chloe-loewe-for-price-fixing/a-74350522 (DW)] [https://www.thefashionlaw.com/eu-slaps-luxury-giants-with-e157m-in-fines-over-illegal-price-controls/ (The Fashion Law)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Dhaka garment factory fire]]
**At least 16 people are killed and several injured in a fire at a [[textile manufacturing|garment factory]] in [[Dhaka]], [[Bangladesh]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/bangladesh-garment-factory-fire-kills-nine-with-toll-likely-rise-official-says-2025-10-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[October 2025 Mexico floods and landslides]]
**The death toll from the past week's torrential rain-related [[flood]]ing across five [[States of Mexico|states]] in eastern [[Mexico]], especially in [[Hidalgo (state)|Hidalgo]] and [[Veracruz]], increases to 64, with 257 others still missing. At least 100,000 homes, 59 medical facilities, and 308 schools across the region are damaged by [[water damage|water]] and [[oil spill|oil]] from the [[Gulf of Mexico]]. [https://www.npr.org/2025/10/14/g-s1-93322/death-toll-torrential-rains-mexico (NPR)] [https://www.milenio.com/estados/veracruz-que-pasa-en-poza-rica-otras-zonas-lluvias-e-indundaciones (''Milenio'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*Twenty people are killed and 16 others are injured when a bus catches fire in [[Rajasthan]], [[India]]. [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] announces compensation payments of [[Indian rupee|₹]]200,000 (US$2,200) to the deceased's families and ₹50,000 ($569) to those injured. [https://apnews.com/article/india-bus-fire-jaisalmer-919667c2c7c7cb84397f9ecfafb05a67 (AP)] [https://www.dw.com/en/india-at-least-20-dead-in-rajasthan-bus-fire/a-74365096 (DW)] [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/rajasthan/jaisalmer-bus-catches-fire-death-injured/article70164003.ece (''The Hindu'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[France–Iran relations]]
**The [[Iran]]ian [[Government of Iran|government]] detains and imprisons two unnamed [[France|French]] nationals for alleged [[espionage]] on behalf of [[List of intelligence agencies of France|French]] and [[Israeli intelligence community|Israeli intelligence agencies]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/iran-jails-2-french-citizens-on-spying-charges/a-74351918 (DW)] [https://www.trtworld.com/article/5ac74e14e7b8 (TRT World)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Castel d'Azzano explosion]]
**Three [[carabinieri]] are killed and 25 other people are injured in an intentional explosion during the attempted [[eviction]] of a [[farmhouse]] in [[Castel d'Azzano]], [[Province of Verona]], [[Veneto]], [[Italy]]. A woman and her two brothers, all in their 60s, are arrested. [https://apnews.com/article/italy-carabinieri-killed-verona-e648aaa872105ec2b8ecd986e80163c0 (AP)] [https://www.rainews.it/maratona/2025/10/esplosione-in-un-casolare-a-castel-dazzano-durante-uno-sgombero-morti-3-carabinieri-217e469e-859f-46fb-9b70-6780755a1013.html (Rai News)]

'''Politics and elections''' 
*[[2025 Malagasy protests]], [[2025 Malagasy coup d'état]]
**[[Madagascar|Malagasy]] [[List of presidents of Madagascar|president]] [[Andry Rajoelina]] issues a decree dissolving the [[National Assembly (Madagascar)|National Assembly]] one day after fleeing to an unknown location, alleging fear for his life following a [[2025 Malagasy coup d'état|military coup]]. [https://apnews.com/article/madagascar-protests-rajoelina-ab1e1eb1aca45fe7e80e81314ebdb0c6 (AP)]
**The National Assembly refuses to comply with Rajoelina's decree and votes to [[Impeachment|impeach]] him, as the [[Madagascar Armed Forces|military]] says that they have now seized power. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/madagascars-president-dissolves-national-assembly-escalating-crisis-2025-10-14/ (Reuters)]
**The [[Madagascar Armed Forces|Malagasy military]] formally announces it is "taking power" with a military council after the ousting of President Rajoelina. [https://www.lemonde.fr/afrique/article/2025/10/14/madagascar-des-militaires-disent-prendre-le-pouvoir-apres-la-destitution-du-president-andry-rajoelina_6646603_3212.html (''Le Monde'')]
*[[2025 Nauruan parliamentary election]]
**Incumbent [[Nauru]]an [[President of Nauru|president]] [[David Adeang]] is unanimously re-elected by the [[Parliament of Nauru|parliament]] following Saturday's election. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/575881/nauru-s-david-adeang-re-elected-as-president-unopposed (RNZ)]
*[[Federal Police (Belgium)|Federal police]] fire [[tear gas]] and [[water cannon]] at over 80,000 demonstrators in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]], protesting against [[Prime Minister of Belgium|Prime Minister]] [[Bart De Wever]]'s proposed [[austerity]] laws which would cut [[pension]]s, [[unemployment benefit]]s, and [[healthcare system]]s in an attempt to lower [[national debt]]. [https://apnews.com/article/belgium-protest-strike-brussels-austerity-measures-3cf5d7f65db2fd25793935432e239e31 (AP)]
*[[President of Peru]] [[José Jerí]] appoints {{ill|Ernesto Álvarez Miranda|es}} as the new [[Prime Minister of Peru|Prime Minister]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/perus-jeri-taps-constitutional-lawyer-new-pm-says-party-leader-2025-10-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Microsoft]] ends support for [[Windows 10]] a decade after its release, despite 41% of [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] users still running this version of the operating system. [https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/windows-10-support-ends-on-october-14-2025-2ca8b313-1946-43d3-b55c-2b95b107f281 (Microsoft)] [https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/microsoft-ends-support-for-windows-10-tuesday-heres-what-you-need-to-know/ (CNET)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]]
**[[South Africa at the FIFA World Cup]]
***In [[association football]], the [[South Africa national soccer team|South Africa soccer team]] [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification|qualifies]] for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|upcoming FIFA World Cup]] following a [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – CAF Group C#Matches|3-0]] win against [[Rwanda national soccer team|Rwanda]]. This will be their first appearance in the [[FIFA World Cup]] since hosting the tournament in [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]]. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/46595773/south-africa-clinch-world-cup-spot-nigeria-playoff (ESPN)]
**[[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]] and [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] also qualify for the upcoming FIFA World Cup. [[Ivory Coast]] will make its first [[Ivory Coast at the FIFA World Cup|appearance in the tournament]] since [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c5ypwvp04nko (BBC)]
